What is the Ordinary Wage (OW) ceiling?
The Ordinary Wage (OW) ceiling sets the maximum amount of OW that attracts CPF contributions in a calendar month for all employees. It was gradually raised and has reached $8,000 in 2026. The increase took place in four steps, as shown in the table below, to allow employers and employees to adjust to the changes.
Table: Changes in CPF salary ceilings
CPF Ordinary Wage ceiling | CPF annual salary ceiling
From 1 Jan 2016 to 31 Aug 2023 | $6,000 | $102,000 (no change)
From 1 Sep to 31 Dec 2023 | $6,300 (+$300)
From 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2024 | $6,800 (+$500)
From 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2025 | $7,400 (+$600)
From 1 Jan 2026 | $8,000 (+$600)

- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports CPF monthly OW and annual AW ceilings): Every employer of an employee who is a citizen of Singapore or a permanent resident shall pay to the Fund monthly contributions at the statutory rates up to the Ordinary Wage monthly ceiling of $8,000, and up to the Additional Wage annual ceiling calculated as $102,000 minus total Ordinary Wages subject to CPF in the year.

**Source:** Examples for computation of Additional Wage (AW) Ceiling (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports CPF monthly OW and annual AW ceilings): Examples for computation of Additional Wage (AW) Ceiling
The AW ceiling determines the maximum amount of AW subject to CPF contributions for the year. An employee’s AW ceiling is computed on a
per employer, per year basis. The AW ceiling applies to all Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents (SPR).
AW ceiling Calculation
The AW ceiling is computed using the following formula:
$102,000 - Total Ordinary Wages (OW) subject to CPF for the year
For the year 2026, the AW ceiling is
$102,000 – ($8,000* x 12)
* The OW ceiling is capped at $8,000 for 2026.
Note: The applicable AW ceiling depends on the due and payable date of the AW. For example, if the 2025 bonus is due and payable to the employee in 2026, then the employer should contribute
according to the 2026 AW ceiling.
Step 1: At every AW payment, e mployers should estimate the AW ceiling by using the current year’s estimated monthly OW. Employers should
either:
a) Submit a refund application online (select the option: Refund of payments made for 1 employee/platform worker) immediately if any excess
contributions on AW are detected; or
b) Pay the shortfall in contributions on AW, if any.
Step 2: In the last month of employment or end of the year in December (whichever is earlier), employers should re-calculate the AW
ceiling based on the actual OW subject to CPF paid up till the last month of employment or in December and pay any shortfall in CPF contributions
together with the employee's contributions for his last month of employment or in December. If there are any excess CPF contributions, you
should submit a refund application online.
For the examples below, we assume that the monthly contribution rates applicable for the employee is for Singaporeans and SPRs (from third
year and onwards). If your employee is a SPR in the first or second year of SPR status, please use the applicable monthly contribution rates.

#### CPF Board — CPF contributions

**Status:** Evidence verified

**CPF newly obtained PR status and OW/AW payable-date treatment** (party in scope: Employee)
- **CPF rule explanation:** The SPR grant date stated for one employee cannot establish another employee’s first-year boundary. The employee who remains a foreigner has no SPR contribution-year boundary until that employee obtains SPR status; the employee’s own Entry Permit date is needed to calculate the boundary. CPF is not payable on the wages of an employee while that employee remains a foreigner. Do not apply another employee’s PR date to this employee’s March OW; a personal contribution amount or boundary is not determined without the employee’s own status date and relevant wage facts. No contribution amount is inferred without those payroll and rate facts. [CPF | Do I need to pay CPF contributions for my foreign employee who has recently obtained Singapore Permanent Residence status?](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/do-i-need-to-pay-cpf-contributions-for-my-foreign-employee-who-has-recently-obtained-singapore-permanent-residence-status)

**Source:** CPF | Do I need to pay CPF contributions for my foreign employee who has recently obtained Singapore Permanent Residence status? (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports CPF newly obtained PR status and OW/AW payable-date treatment): SOURCE CAPTURE METADATA
Authority: CPF Board, Government of Singapore
Page title: Do I need to pay CPF contributions for my foreign employee who has recently obtained Singapore Permanent Residence status?
Canonical official URL: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/do-i-need-to-pay-cpf-contributions-for-my-foreign-employee-who-has-recently-obtained-singapore-permanent-residence-status
Capture date (Singapore): 2026-11-01
Capture method: official web read visible-text excerpt; raw HTML was not retained. Source lines 138–191 and continuation, independently opened via web tool. This excerpt is not a native HTTP response.

Yes, CPF contributions are payable once your foreign employee obtains his Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status. Please ensure that your employee informs you of his SPR status.
For the first two years of obtaining the SPR status, to help your employee adjust to the lower take-home pay, both you and your SPR employee will contribute CPF at graduated rates (refer to Tables 2 and 3). From the third year onwards, you and your SPR employee will contribute CPF at the full rates (refer to Table 1).
Determining your employee’s year of SPR status
The year of SPR status determines your employee’s CPF contribution rates.
First-year rate: Applies from the day your employee obtains his SPR status until the last day of the month of his first anniversary. The SPR status date is shown on his Entry Permit (Form 5/5A) issued by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA).
Second-year rate: Applies from the month following his first anniversary as an SPR until the last day of the month of his second anniversary.
Third-year rate: Applies from the month following his second anniversary as an SPR onwards.
Example
If your employee obtained his SPR status on 15 January 2026, the start and end dates for first, second and third year of obtaining SPR status are shown in the table below:
Years of obtaining SPR status | Starts from | Ends on
First year | 15 January 2026 | 31 January 2027
Second year | 1 February 2027 | 31 January 2028
Third year | 1 February 2028 | Not applicable
Computing CPF contributions
For Ordinary Wages (OW), you will need to pay CPF contributions on the pro-rated OW. For Additional Wages (AW), CPF contributions are required depending on when the AW is payable to your employee.
Example
Assuming your employee obtains his SPR status on 15 March 2026 and he receives OW and AW for March 2026.
For OW
CPF contribution is required on the pro-rated wages from 15 to 31 March 2026.
For AW
• CPF contribution is not required on the AW if it is payable while the employee was a foreigner i.e. before 15 March 2026.
• CPF contribution is required on the AW if it is payable on or after 15 March 2026.

outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

#### CPF Board — CPF contributions

**Status:** Evidence verified

**CPF permanent resident contribution year timing** (party in scope: Employee)
- **CPF rule explanation:** For PR status obtained on 15/03/2026, first-year rates apply from that date through 31/03/2027; second-year rates apply from 01/04/2027 through 31/03/2028; third-year rates start 01/04/2028. As a Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR), you are required to make CPF contributions on wages earned in Singapore.
CPF contributions are not payable for employees who are neither Singapore Citizens nor SPRs.
Your CPF contribution rates as an SPR depend on how long you have held Permanent Resident status.
First-year rate: Applies from the day you obtain your SPR status, [i.e. the date indicated on your Entry Permit (Form 5/5A) issued by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA)] until the last day of the month of your first anniversary of SPR.
Second-year rate: Applies from the month following your first anniversary as an SPR until the last day of the month of your second anniversary.
Third-year rate: Applies from the month following your second anniversary as an SPR onwards.
Example
If you have obtained your SPR status on 15 January 2026, the start and end dates for first, second and third year of obtaining SPR status are shown in the table below:
Year of obtaining SPR status | Starts from | Ends on
First year | 15 January 2026 | 31 January 2027
Second year | 1 February 2027 | 31 January 2028
Third year | 1 February 2028 | Not applicable

- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports CPF permanent resident contribution year timing): Yes, CPF contributions are payable once your foreign employee obtains his Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status. Please ensure that your employee informs you of his SPR status.
For the first two years of obtaining the SPR status, to help your employee adjust to the lower take-home pay, both you and your SPR employee will contribute CPF at graduated rates (refer to Tables 2 and 3). From the third year onwards, you and your SPR employee will contribute CPF at the full rates (refer to Table 1).
Determining your employee’s year of SPR status
The year of SPR status determines your employee’s CPF contribution rates.
First-year rate: Applies from the day your employee obtains his SPR status until the last day of the month of his first anniversary. The SPR status date is shown on his Entry Permit (Form 5/5A) issued by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA).
Second-year rate: Applies from the month following his first anniversary as an SPR until the last day of the month of his second anniversary.
Third-year rate: Applies from the month following his second anniversary as an SPR onwards.
Example
If your employee obtained his SPR status on 15 January 2026, the start and end dates for first, second and third year of obtaining SPR status are shown in the table below:
Years of obtaining SPR status | Starts from | Ends on
First year | 15 January 2026 | 31 January 2027
Second year | 1 February 2027 | 31 January 2028
Third year | 1 February 2028 | Not applicable
Computing CPF contributions
For Ordinary Wages (OW), you will need to pay CPF contributions on the pro-rated OW. For Additional Wages (AW), CPF contributions are required depending on when the AW is payable to your employee.
Example
Assuming your employee obtains his SPR status on 15 March 2026 and he receives OW and AW for March 2026.
For OW
CPF contribution is required on the pro-rated wages from 15 to 31 March 2026.
For AW
• CPF contribution is not required on the AW if it is payable while the employee was a foreigner i.e. before 15 March 2026.
• CPF contribution is required on the AW if it is payable on or after 15 March 2026.
